question: Which of the following phyla of animals have jointed legs?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arthropod**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Arthropods** are a phylum of invertebrate animals having an exoskeleton, a segmented body, and jointed appendages.
 
• The phylum Arthropoda includes insects, arachnids, myriapods, and crustaceans.
 
• Arthropods are characterized by their jointed legs, which enable them to have greater mobility and adaptability in various environments.
 
• They are the largest phylum in the animal kingdom, encompassing more than 80% of all described species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phylum Echinodermata**

 
 
• This phylum includes marine animals like starfish, sea urchins, and sand dollars.
 
• Echinoderms have a unique water vascular system used for locomotion and feeding.
 
• They exhibit radial symmetry as adults, which is different from the bilateral symmetry seen in arthropods.
 
 
 
• **Phylum Annelida**
 
 
• Annelids include segmented worms like earthworms, leeches, and polychaetes.
 
• They have a segmented body but lack jointed appendages.
 
• Annelids have a coelom, a fluid-filled body cavity that provides a hydrostatic skeleton.
 
 
 
• **Phylum Nematoda**
 
 
• Nematodes, or roundworms, are unsegmented worms with a cylindrical body.
 
• They have a complete digestive system but lack jointed appendages.
 
• Many nematodes are parasitic, affecting plants, animals, and humans.
